'''James Hamilton McLean''' (17 June 1936 – 11 November 2016)<ref>Coan E. V., Kabat A. R. & Petit R. E. (15 February 2009) [http://www.malacological.org/publications/2400_malacology.php ''2,400 years of Malacology''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121111161316/http://www.malacological.org/publications/2400_malacology.php |date=2012-11-11 }} (6th Edition).</ref> was an American [[malacologist]] (a [[biologist]] who studies [[mollusk]]s). He specialized in [[marine (ocean)|marine]] [[gastropod]]s. He worked on many families of Eastern Pacific gastropods including the [[Fissurellidae]], [[Trochidae]], [[Turbinidae]] and [[Liotiidae]], and also investigated deep sea gastropods from [[hydrothermal vent]]s.<ref name="nhm.org"/>

McLean worked as a curator of the [[Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County]] from 1964 to 2001 and was a curator emeritus there until his death in November 2016.<ref name="nhm.org"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=James Hamilton McLean |url=https://bionomia.net/Q1680519 |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=bionomia.net |language=en}}</ref>

== Molluscs described ==
McLean, often together with other malacologists, described, according to the database [[WoRMS]], 385 new taxa.<ref name="nhm.org">(7 December 2007) {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/*/www.nhm.org/research/malacology/mclean.html |date=* |title=''James McLean: Emeritus Curator'' webpage }} from [[Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County]] website</ref>

At least 37 taxa were named for James McLean with the epithet ''macleani'' (according to WoRMS)

He named numerous taxa of marine [[gastropods]] including:
* [[Clypeosectidae]] McLean, 1989, a family of [[hydrothermal vent]] limpets
